idiom_name: amqplib channel.publish(exchange, routingKey, body) plus broker bindings on a topic exchange
implementation_notes: In Node the routing decision is expressed as broker topology rather than as an application class: assert a topic exchange, bind each consumer queue with a binding key (* substitutes one word, # zero or more) and publish with channel.publish(exchange, routingKey, buffer) where the key encodes the routing metadata (for example facility.severity). The broker performs the fan-out to every matching binding, so the Router object disappears; the same publish call with a direct exchange routes on exact key equality and with a fanout exchange broadcasts. Replace the classic structure with this whenever a broker is already in the stack; a Map from route key to handler function is the honest in-process substitute only when adding a broker solely for routing would be over-engineering.
pitfalls: A routing key that matches no binding is discarded by the broker without an error - configure an alternate exchange or a dead-letter exchange and monitor it.
Bindings are durable broker state: an old queue binding keeps receiving messages long after its consumer is gone.
Messages published before a queue is bound are lost (unroutable messages are not stored by default), so declaration order matters at startup.
Fan-out delivers one copy per matching queue with at-least-once semantics, so consumers must be idempotent or duplicates will be processed.
